Horton Plains has the largest known population and happens also to be the only known habitat of an endemic shrimp Caridina singhalensis. This shrimp is now extremely rare and its survival depends on the expeditious elimination of the rainbow trout from its habitats. Its introduction also promoted the extermination by anglers of the otter(Lutra lutra), which was thought to prey on this fish. However, otters have survived this threat and are still found in trout streams. Fishing the trout requires license. Also Ref. 1739, 43638.

Known from the eastern drainages of Sri Lanka, primarily the major basins of Gal Oya, Kumbukkan Oya, and Menik Ganga, The highest elevation where the species was found was at 690 m asl, in Ibbanna Oya, near Lunugala. The populations found from the eastern slopes of the Knuckles hills draining to Mahaweli River and its floodplain exhibit several morphological disparities (Ref. 123756).

Type locality of Ophiocephalus marulius ara, neotype in Mahaweli River basin, Angammedilla. Known from the middle and lower regions of the Mahaweli basin, occurs primarily in the deep pools in the Mahaweli River and its tributaries; also recorded from reservoirs in the Mahaweli catchment (Victoria and Randenigala). Around 20 juveniles (ca. 8.0-10.0 cm SL), guarded by a pair of adults, were observed in shallow water (ca. 60-80 cm deep), among submerged roots, close to the bank, at the mouth of a stream draining into Badulu Oya of the Mahaweli basin. The highest recorded elevation from which it was found was about 500 m asl at Kandy (Ref. 127648).
Type locality of Devario memorialis, Ma Oya basin, Aranayake (Ref. 127711).

Type locality of Laubuka hema, Gal Oya basin, Nilgala. Occurs mainly from the headwaters of the Gal basin in the Kotagama and Nilgala areas (194-294 m asl), with a single specimen collected from the headwaters of Hepola stream in Bibile, which drains to the Mahaweli River (Ref. 127713).

Type locality of Labeo heladiva, Attanagalu Oya basin, Uruwal Oya (Ref. 118635). Population is reported to be declining probably due to competition with the introduced fish Oreochromis mossambicus (Ref. 6028). Caught with same gear in fishing for Oreochromis mossambicus (Ref. 36778).
It is widely distributed in the country, occurring in the lowlands of both the dry and the wet zones of the island (Ref. 124133).

Type locality of Schistura scripta, Nakiyadeniya in the south-western lowlands of Sri Lanka. It is known only from its type locality, a stream about 3-4 m wide, flowing through the palm-oil plantations of Nakiyadeniya Estate in an unprotected area of the Gin River basin, elevation ca. 80 m above sea level; substrate consists of small boulders and pebbles. It prefers the faster-flowing regions of the stream and was observed with Garra ceylonensis, Rasbora dandia, Belontia signata. It appears to be locally abundant when sampled during a relatively dry period in December 2017 and about 100 adults, including several gravid females, were observed in a stretch of approximately 50 m along the length of the stream. Schistura notostigma was recorded in similar habitats sampled in Udugama about 8 km from the type locality of S. scripta and as presently understood, these two species do not co-occur (Ref. 127984).
Type locality of Lophiodes lugubris, 13.5 miles north 64° west of Columbo Light House (Ref. 128445).
